title: Prove free basis changes keep the right-vector diagonal count (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped proof, with finite controls. No new κ.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

Factors are `I + u y^T` with `u` in `R^n` and `y` in `K^n`, over any field `K` and any associative `K`-algebra `R`. Free maps are arbitrary `GL_n(K)` changes of basis anywhere in the word. The exact number of factors for `diag(d)` is

```text
t_K(d) = #{ i : d_i is not in K^x }
```

Over `F_2` this is `t`, the count of entries different from 1. So free `GL_n(F_2)` mixing never realizes a diagonal with fewer than `t` factors. That answers open question 1 of `research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum` (#4099), which proved the count without free maps and named the missing invariant as the blocker.

Proof, in `PROOF.md`:

1. Conjugating a factor by a free map gives a factor, so every word equals `Q S` with `Q` a product of `L` factors and `S` in `GL_n(K)`.
2. The column bound from #4099: `Q - I` maps `K^n` into a `K`-space spanned by `L` vectors.
3. A new kernel lemma: for a diagonal `D` and any `T` in `GL_n(K)`, every kernel vector of `D T - I` on `K^n` vanishes at each `i` with `d_i` not in `K^x`. So `t_K(d) <= dim (D T - I) K^n <= L`.

Coordinate factors plus one free diagonal map attain the bound. As a corollary, every group algebra `F_2[G]`, abelian or not, has exact diagonal minimum `t` in the full nonidentity-label alphabet with free scalar mixing. Restricted label sets, such as `{i, j}` in `F_2[Q8]`, are outside the statement.

Package: `research/right-vector-diagonal-free-basis`. Base `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19081206

## Evidence

`verify.py` uses the standard library, writes nothing, and runs in about 20 seconds per mode. All of the following pass locally:

- Exhaustive free-map word searches at `n = 2`. `F_2[C_2 x C_2]` up to two factors: all 256 diagonals are reached, each first at length `t`. `F_2[S_3]`, which is nonabelian, up to one factor: 127 diagonals. `F_3[x]/(x^2)` up to one factor with all 48 maps in `GL_2(F_3)`: 32 diagonals, each first at length `t_K`.
- Every conjugate of every factor stays in the alphabet (93,720 checks).
- The kernel lemma holds in 718,128 (diagonal, free map) cases, over the three rings at `n = 2` and the Klein ring at `n = 3`.
- Over `F_3`, `diag(2,2)` is free (length 0). #4099's ring-valued right-vector witness lies outside the alphabet and gives `t = 2` from one factor.
- The normal and `-O` runs print the same receipt, `0e2493f91a52d1bdacfa78d79f3dc634782fbbff71bab7c5040adb0d2444f849`.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B -W error research/right-vector-diagonal-free-basis/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -B -W error research/right-vector-diagonal-free-basis/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/right-vector-diagonal-free-basis
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/right-vector-diagonal-free-basis --check-source-history
```

## Limitations and unrun obligations

This is an exact count in a formal alphabet. Native frames, hosting, routing, precision and recursive cost are not priced, and no supplier changes. Free maps must have entries in `K`; with `R`-valued free maps nothing is claimed. The finite searches are corroboration only. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No selected-result, Lean or Docker replay was run.

## Open next questions

1. For a non-diagonal target `M`, is the minimum `min_T dim_K (M T - I) K^n`? The lower bound follows from the same normal form. The upper bound needs a factorization with invertible prefixes.
2. Which restricted label sets keep a count above `t` once free scalar mixing is allowed? Start by adding one label outside `{i, j}` in `F_2[Q8]` for a single `[zi]` target.
3. Bind one coordinate word to an existing supplier meter.

## Related open work

- #3906 audits the Q8 dirty-spectator restoration boundary with paid labels `{i, j}` only. Its one- and two-target counts, 3 and 6, are in a restricted alphabet. In the full label alphabet this theorem gives 1 and 2. The numbers concern different alphabets and are not compared as equal. They are consistent, because restricting labels can only raise the count.
- No open PR addresses #4099's open question 1 (checked open PR titles and bodies, `scripts/find_overlap.py`, and #1166).

No check failed. All four reproduction commands also passed locally (CPython 3.12, macOS arm64), about 20 s per verifier mode.
